GuardDuty ingests events from separate, independent data sources to provide comprehensive security value.\\n\\n**Important:**\\n\\nYour individual service log configuration or filtering rules (for VPC Flow Logs, DNS Logs, CloudTrail Events, S3 Data Events, Kubernetes Audit Logs, and Lambda Network Logs) do not impact the logs/events processed by GuardDuty.\\n\\n### GuardDuty VPC Flow Logs processing charges for instances monitored by GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring\\n\\nFor instances monitored by GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring (via either EC2 Runtime agent or Amazon EKS Runtime agent), GuardDuty will not charge for VPC Flow Logs processing as long as the agent actively sends runtime event data. If the agent stops transmitting event data, GuardDuty reverts to charging via VPC Flow Logs.\\n\\nEnabling Runtime Monitoring decreases VPC Flow Logs usage in GuardDuty Amazon CloudWatch usage metrics. Disabling Runtime Monitoring restores VPC Flow Logs usage\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/monitoring_costs.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Get to know Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring for Amazon EC2 | AWS Security Blog\",\"context\":\"### Runtime data and flow logs data\\n\\nWhen exploring the Runtime Monitoring feature and its usefulness for your organization, a key item to understand is the foundational level of protection for your account and workloads. When you enable GuardDuty the foundational data sources of VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail logs are also enabled, and those sources cannot be turned off without fully disabling GuardDuty. Runtime Monitoring provides contextual information that allows for more precise findings that can help with targeted remediation compared to the information provided in VPC Flow Logs. When the Runtime Monitoring agent is deployed onto an instance, the GuardDuty service still processes the VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs for that instance. If, at any point in time, an unauthorized user tampers with your security agent or an instance is deployed without the security agent, GuardDuty will continue to use VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs data to monitor for potential threats and suspicious activity, providing you defense in depth to help ensure you have visibility and coverage for detecting threats.\\n\\n> **Note**: GuardDuty doesn\u2019t charge you for processing VPC Flow Logs while the Runtime Monitoring agent is active on an instance\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/get-to-know-amazon-guardduty-runtime-monitoring-for-amazon-ec2/\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How it works\",\"context\":\"# How it works\\n\\nTo use Runtime Monitoring, you must enable Runtime Monitoring and then manage the GuardDuty security agent. The\\nfollowing list explains this two-step process:\\n\\n1. **Enable Runtime Monitoring** for your account so that GuardDuty can accept\\n the runtime events that it receives from your Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon ECS clusters, and Amazon EKS\\n workloads.\\n2. **Manage GuardDuty agent** for the individual resources for which you\\n want to monitor the runtime behavior. Based on the resource type, you can choose to:\\n\\n * Use automated agent configuration, where GuardDuty manages the agent deployment and automatically creates a Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC)\\n endpoint.\\n * Install agent manually, which requires you to create the VPC endpoint as a prerequisite.\\n\\n The security agent uses a VPC endpoint to deliver events to GuardDuty, ensuring that the data remains\\n within the AWS network. This approach enhances security and allows GuardDuty to monitor and analyze runtime behavior\\n across your resources (Amazon EKS, Amazon EC2, and AWS Fargate-Amazon ECS). GuardDuty uses Instance identity roles that authenticate the security agent for each resource type\\n to send the associated runtime events to the VPC endpoint.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nGuardDuty analyzes runtime events in your AWS environment, uses them internally for threat detection, and presents the results through findings.\\n\\nWhen you manage the security agent (either manually or through GuardDuty) in EKS Runtime Monitoring\\nor Runtime Monitoring for EC2 instances, and\\nGuardDuty is presently deployed on an Amazon EC2 instance and receives\\nthe Collected runtime event\\ntypes from this instance, GuardDuty will not charge\\nyour AWS account for the analysis of VPC flow logs from this Amazon EC2 instance. This helps GuardDuty avoid double usage cost in the account.\\n\\nThe following topics explain how enabling Runtime Monitoring and managing GuardDuty security agent works\\ndifferently for each resource type.\\n\\n###### Contents\\n\\n* How Runtime Monitoring works with Amazon EKS clusters\\n* How Runtime Monitoring works with Amazon EC2 instances\\n* How Runtime Monitoring works with Fargate (Amazon ECS only)\\n* After you enable Runtime Monitoring\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/how-does-runtime-monitoring-work.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up AWS docs on GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring and VPC Flow Log cost impact."}

{"id": "bdfac382-c3a4-4dff-8a7f-9efd4be4c970", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Quick clarification: there's no "GuardDuty cost optimization skill" in my available tools, so I pulled this straight from AWS documentation instead. Here's what it says:

For instances actively monitored by GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring (via the EC2 or EKS runtime agent), **GuardDuty stops charging for VPC Flow Log processing on those instances** as long as the agent is actively sending runtime event data. GuardDuty still technically processes/uses the VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs for that instance as a defense-in-depth fallback, but you aren't billed for that processing while the agent is active — this avoids double-charging you for overlapping coverage.

A few important nuances:
- If the agent stops transmitting data (e.g., tampered with, or an instance is deployed without it), GuardDuty reverts to charging for VPC Flow Log processing on that instance.
- This shows up concretely in usage metrics: enabling Runtime Monitoring decreases VPC Flow Logs usage in GuardDuty's CloudWatch usage metrics, and disabling it restores that usage.
- DNS Logs and CloudTrail remain foundational data sources that can't be turned off while GuardDuty itself is enabled.

If you'd like, I can look at whether Runtime Monitoring is enabled in your account and check what your actual VPC Flow Logs usage looks like.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
